description: Active Directory Domain Admin, Enterprise Admin, Schema Admin and equivalent tier-0 directory roles with control over the identity fabric; the top lateral-movement target
typical_secrets: AD passwords; Kerberos TGT/keys; NTLM hashes; smartcard PINs

description: Built-in or named local Administrator on Windows servers and workstations; frequently shares a common password across the estate (LAPS gap)
typical_secrets: Local SAM password hashes; LAPS-managed passwords; cached credentials

description: root and uid-0 equivalents on Unix/Linux hosts; direct or via sudo/su; highest-privilege account on the platform
typical_secrets: root password; SSH private keys; sudoers entries

description: Privileged DBA principals (Oracle SYS/SYSTEM, SQL Server sa/sysadmin, PostgreSQL superuser, MySQL root) with schema, data and audit-config control
typical_secrets: DB passwords; wallet credentials; client certs; privileged DB roles

description: Non-human application/system service account (svc_-prefixed, daemon, batch) running services, scheduled tasks and middleware; rarely rotated, often over-privileged
typical_secrets: Static passwords; SSH keys; API keys; Kerberos keytabs

description: Embedded/hard-coded credential an application uses to authenticate to another application, database or middleware; the classic vaulting/brokering target
typical_secrets: Hard-coded passwords; connection-string secrets; API keys; client certs

description: Highly privileged cloud identity (AWS root/Administrator/OrganizationAccountAccessRole, Azure Global Admin/Owner, GCP Organization Admin) governed via CIEM
typical_secrets: Long-lived access keys; STS/assume-role tokens; managed-identity tokens; service-account keys

description: Privileged administrator of routers, switches, firewalls, load-balancers and SD-WAN edges, often via TACACS+/RADIUS or local enable accounts
typical_secrets: Enable/secret passwords; SSH keys; TACACS+ shared secrets; SNMPv3 creds

description: Privileged admin of the virtualization layer (VMware vCenter/ESXi, Hyper-V, Nutanix, KVM) with control over all guest workloads and snapshots
typical_secrets: vCenter/ESXi credentials; SSO admin passwords; host root passwords

description: Tenant super-administrator of a SaaS or management console (M365 Global Admin, Okta super admin, Salesforce sys admin, ServiceNow admin, Workday security admin)
typical_secrets: Console passwords; MFA tokens; API admin keys; SAML/OIDC admin sessions

description: Build/deploy pipeline identity holding deploy credentials and able to push to production; high blast-radius supply-chain target
typical_secrets: Pipeline secrets; deploy keys; cloud deploy roles; OIDC tokens; PATs

description: Group Managed Service Account or SPN-bound Kerberos service account for Windows services; Kerberoasting and delegation-abuse target
typical_secrets: gMSA auto-managed passwords; Kerberos keytabs/SPNs; msDS-ManagedPassword

description: Highly privileged emergency-access account (cloud-only Global Admin, root recovery) reserved for outages and incident response; excluded from conditional access
typical_secrets: Sealed long passwords; offline credential envelopes; recovery keys; FIDO2 keys

description: Business user with privileged entitlements in line-of-business systems (payments approver, GL/journal poster, treasury operator, core-banking admin) — privileged by function, not IT role
typical_secrets: Application passwords; MFA tokens; signing credentials

description: External vendor, MSP or contractor identity granted privileged remote access for support and maintenance; major supply-chain and standing-access risk
typical_secrets: VPN/remote-session credentials; vendor PAM credentials; shared support passwords

description: Privileged operator of the secrets-management or PAM platform itself (Vault admin, CyberArk Vault/PVWA admin, safe owner); compromise yields the keys to the kingdom
typical_secrets: Vault root/admin tokens; recovery (Shamir) shares; safe-owner credentials; master keys

description: Backup and disaster-recovery service identity (NetBackup, Commvault, Veeam, Rubrik, Cohesity) with cross-system read and restore rights; prime ransomware target
typical_secrets: Privileged AD service accounts; hypervisor admin creds; immutable-storage/object-lock tokens

description: z/OS RACF/ACF2/Top Secret special/operations IDs, started-task and CICS region IDs, AS/400 *SECOFR profiles with system-wide authority
typical_secrets: RACF passphrases; IBM MFA tokens; certs in RACF keyrings; SPECIAL/OPERATIONS attributes

description: Over-permissioned non-human cloud workload role/principal (EC2 instance profile, Lambda exec role, GKE workload identity) flagged by CIEM as holding privileged or unused entitlements
typical_secrets: Instance-profile STS tokens; managed-identity tokens; workload-identity-federation tokens

description: Workload granted just-in-time privileged access after attestation, with no stored standing secret (SPIFFE/SPIRE-attested, broker-issued); the zero-standing-privilege target state for machine access
typical_secrets: Short-lived attested tokens; X.509-SVIDs; broker-issued ephemeral credentials

description: An LLM-driven or agent-delegated identity that performs privileged actions on behalf of a human owner — requesting just-in-time elevation, opening brokered privileged sessions, and running privileged tools. The agentic analogue of a privileged operator; in the good state it holds no standing privileged credential and acts only through the broker.
typical_secrets: Brokered short-lived privileged-session tokens; OAuth on-behalf-of tokens; JIT-issued ephemeral credentials (no standing privileged secret)
